item.title: UK moves to sanction Israeli settlements as PM Burnham risks clash with Trump: report
item.description: Andy Burnham's UK sanctions targeting Israeli West Bank settlements spark fierce backlash from Benjamin Netanyahu's ministers and U.S. lawmakers.
item.content:encoded:
The United Kingdom is expected to announce restrictions targeting trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank on Tuesday, a move already drawing strong pushback Monday from U.S. and Israeli officials.

According to The Times, a US State Department said Washington was "tracking the plans closely."

The measures are expected to include an embargo on goods and some services involving West Bank settlements marking an escalation in London’s pressure on Israel under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has taken a firmer stance on the conflict, according to reports.

The announcement is expected to come a day after Burnham spoke by phone with President Donald Trump.

WHO IS ANDY BURNHAM? BRITAIN'S NEW PRIME MINISTER AND LONGTIME TRUMP CRITIC

According to a No. 10 Downing Street readout of the call Monday, the two leaders discussed the Middle East, with Burnham highlighting the importance of a two-state solution which calls for an independent Palestinian state comprising the West Bank and Gaza Strip to exist alongside Israel.

"On the Middle East, the Prime Minister set out the UK’s commitment to working towards peace and security in the region, stressing the importance of the Two-State Solution," the spokesperson said.

The readout did not mention the planned sanctions. Bloomberg reported, however, that the timing of the call suggested Burnham may have briefed Trump on the measures targeting goods and services linked to Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

The move could create an early point of friction between Burnham and Washington, where the Trump administration has strongly backed Israel, the outlet said.

I’M AN ARAB MUSLIM — I STILL DON’T UNDERSTAND THE ANTISEMITIC BDS MOVEMENT

The new measures, billed widely as sanctions, are expected to be formally unveiled by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who has already pledged a "comprehensive reset" of Britain’s policy toward Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

Miliband signaled last week that measures were coming in response to Israeli settlement expansion, including the E1 project east of Jerusalem, according to The National.

He went on to describe E1 as a longstanding "red line" and said Britain would take action to protect the prospect of a two-state solution.

The planned sanction announcement has already drawn sharp criticism in Israel and the United States.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the British ambassador’s expulsion in a post on X.

"We will not be a doormat for an antisemitic government in a country occupied by radical Islam that is trying to escape economic and social collapse by attacking Jews and the State of Israel," Smotrich wrote. "The British Mandate in Israel is over."

EX-PENTAGON OFFICIAL URGES US TO ‘SQUEEZE’ UK ON DEFENSE AMID FALKLANDS FUROR

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir also condemned the planned restrictions, writing in Spanish on X that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should retaliate by recognizing Argentine sovereignty over the Falkland Islands and imposing sanctions on Britain.

Ben-Gvir accused Britain of having "violently" taken the disputed islands, known in Argentina as the Malvinas, the Times of Israel reported.

In the United States, Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., also warned in a post on X that the planned measures could implicate Florida’s anti-boycott law and potentially prevent some affected British companies from doing business with state and local governments.

Meanwhile, Burnham has joined leaders from Canada, France, Germany, Italy and other countries in condemning Israel’s E1 settlement expansion, arguing that the project threatens the viability of a future Palestinian state.

item.title: FSU-SMU game turns into old-school football after stadium power outage wipes out in-game communication
item.description: A power outage plunged Doak Campbell Stadium into darkness minutes before kickoff, forcing SMU and Florida State to play without communications.
item.content:encoded:
Just when we thought the college football weekend couldn’t get any crazier, a power outage at Doak Campbell Stadium on the campus of Florida State sent school officials into a frenzy on Monday night in Tallahassee.

Minutes before SMU and FSU were set to close out Labor Day weekend with there ACC game to finish week one, the lights went out inside the stadium that forced both teams back into the locker room.

The game was scheduled to kickoff at 7:39 p.m. ET, but a power surge sent the stadium into darkness just as both teams had taking the field.

Trust me, the jokes could write themselves for Florida State, but this unfortunate set of circumstances for everyone involved turned into a chaotic night.

A very critical decision awaited, knowing there would also be no official replay during the game if both schools decided to play

.

Every twenty minutes, officials from both schools and ACC commissioner Jim Phillips were meeting to discuss possible outcomes if they weren’t able to play the game on Monday night.

For the fans, credit to them for sticking around through the madness, with games being played in the stands and the Florida State marching band trying their best to keep them all engaged. But, this was a mess.

At 8:45 ET, following a third meeting between officials, the decision was made to play the game on Monday night without any type of communications. This included helmet-to-helmet comms, communication between coordinators or iPad usage along the sideline.

Simply put, both teams decided to go full old-school tonight in Tallahassee.

MICHIGAN-WESTERN MICHIGAN CLOCK CONTROVERSY LEAVES PLAYERS, FANS AND A RULES ANALYST PUZZLED

The officials were having to practice hand signals with the coaches from both teams at 9:06 p.m. ET, while stadium officials were praying that the power would be fully-restored by the second half at the very least.

I've seen some things covering this sport, but tonight is up their on the list on wildest events that have taken place in the past twenty years on the field.

Both teams decided it would be a wise move to play without communications that are key for everyone involved in a college football game.

And, sources told OutKick that there would have been an ample amount of problems for SMU to play this game on Tuesday. The Mustangs host UC Davis on Saturday, while the Seminoles have the weekend off.

So, pushing this game back a day might have been the smart move, but would have been challenging for Rhett Lashlee and his football program. Also, you cannot just reschedule the game for later in the season for obvious reasons.

The outcome was crucial for Florida State head coach Mike Norvell, who was already feeling the heat coming into the season.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee noted that his team had not practiced without coach-to-player communication in over two years, so tonight was the first time since 2024 that he had not been in communication with his quarterback during a game.

Even though both teams were dealing with the same problems Monday night, the result of this decision to play was going to haunt one of these coaches.

In the end, this might have been fun for the fans inside Doak Campbell Stadium and those watching at home.

But this was a massive gamble for SMU and Florida State to play this game Monday night, with so much on the line.

item.title: Popular TV host, media star faces hanging after conviction in major synthetic drug trafficking case
item.description: Sarah Khalifa was among 12 defendants sentenced to death after prosecutors accused the group of manufacturing and trafficking synthetic narcotics.
item.content:encoded:
A popular Egyptian TV host on Saturday was sentenced to death by hanging in a major drug case that accused dozens of suspects of forming an organized criminal group to manufacture and traffic synthetic drugs.

Sarah Khalifa is among 12 defendants facing execution for their alleged roles in the operation, including importing materials used to produce narcotics, according to state-backed media Ahram Online. Capital punishment in Egypt is carried out by hanging for civilian convictions.

Khalifa is a media personality, beauty clinic owner and former TV host who has appeared on several Egyptian television channels. Local outlet Masrawy reported that she previously hosted the Egyptian crime show "Mission Impossible."

Khalifa, who currently has more than 2.5 million followers on Instagram, was reportedly arrested in Cairo in April 2025 as part of the investigation.

DOCTOR AND SON ACCUSED OF RUNNING DANGEROUS SIDE-BUSINESS SCHEME IN NEW YORK

The case involved a total of 28 defendants who were charged with forming an organized criminal group, as well as possessing unlicensed firearms and ammunition, Ahram Online said. Twelve were sentenced to death, nine received life sentences and seven were acquitted of all charges.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRACKS DOWN ON BRAZIL'S BIGGEST DRUG GANGS WITH ‘GLOBAL TERROR’ DESIGNATION

The group allegedly operated like a production and distribution network, with members assigned different roles. Some were responsible for importing raw materials, while others manufactured and distributed the synthetic drugs, the prosecution said, according to reports.

The group was also accused of storing materials and manufacturing drugs in a residential property.

More than 750 kilograms, or roughly 1,653 pounds, of synthetic narcotics and raw materials were seized during the investigation, prosecutors said, according to reports.

The case against Khalifa and the other defendants relied on statements from 20 witnesses, along with technical and digital evidence, including messages, photographs and videos that prosecutors said documented the alleged criminal activity, according to Ahram Online.

Authorities also placed the defendants' assets and bank accounts under precautionary measures and ordered those already in custody to remain detained, Ahram Online reported.

item.title: Climber dies in fatal fall on Colorado 14er south of Aspen
item.description: A 21-member rescue team was dispatched to the remote mountain after nearby hikers witnessed the climber fall and officials determined the injuries were not survivable.
item.content:encoded:
Officials in Colorado said a climber suffered a fatal fall Sunday after scaling a towering peak south of Aspen.

The tragic incident occurred on Castle Peak, which reaches a steep elevation of 14,272 feet in the Elk Mountains, according to Mountain Rescue Aspen.

Responders said rescue team members reached the climber by 4 p.m. after the Gunnison County Sheriff's Office was notified of a fallen climber.

However, officials "determined the individual had sustained injuries that were not survivable."

NORTH CAROLINA CLIMBER AIRLIFTED AFTER PLUNGING 20 FEET DOWN GORGE, SUSTAINING SERIOUS INJURIES

The fall was apparently witnessed by nearby hikers, including Rebecca Rees, who recounted the incident in a statement posted to Facebook.

"Unfortunately, we witnessed the event. It has been an extremely sad and terrible afternoon for all involved. He did not survive," she said.

Rees said a bystander, identified as Robert, even scrambled toward the climber immediately after the fall, putting himself at risk in case there was still a chance of survival.

She added that the victim ultimately "wasn’t alone" in his final moments.

NOVICE CLIMBER SURVIVES 1,500-FOOT DROP ON CALIFORNIA'S MOUNT SHASTA AFTER HELICOPTER RESCUE DELAYED BY CLOUDS

Rees said the rescue crew responded at a commendable speed. Despite the remote location, helicopter and ground teams reportedly reached nearly 13,000 feet in under two hours on a holiday weekend.

According to Mountain Rescue Aspen, officials used off-highway vehicles and helicopters to reach the remote area.

After a helicopter located the fallen climber, it returned to Aspen to pick up additional rescue personnel before taking them to the high-elevation area near the peak.

MOUNTAIN CLIMBER SURVIVES TERRIFYING 500-FOOT FALL IN CALIFORNIA'S SIERRA NEVADA, NIGHT STRANDED ON LEDGE

A total of 21 rescue members were sent into the field, and officials safely recovered and evacuated the deceased climber from the mountain shortly after 8 p.m.

Rees said the responders showed extraordinary compassion throughout the recovery effort.

"The response of search and rescue, the sheriff, and the coroner all made us feel like every single person matters. This young man had a story and we all care," she said.

item.title: Aaron Judge returns to Yankees after 83 games missed with rib injury ahead of postseason push
item.description: The New York Yankees activated Aaron Judge from the 60-day injured list after a broken rib, skipping a rehab assignment ahead of the Rockies series.
item.content:encoded:
The Bronx Bombers are getting their captain back.

Aaron Judge is making his long-awaited return from the 60-day injured list, as the New York Yankees announced his reinstatement ahead of their series against the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium.

Judge has spent the last three months on the injured list with a stress fracture in his right first rib, which he suffered in late May.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

On Monday, Judge was seen working out at Yankee Stadium, facing live batting practice and hitting the ball all over the field, indicating he was healthy enough to go against big league arms.

In fact, the Yankees opted not to give Judge a minor-league rehab assignment. Manager Aaron Boone noted there were more creative ways to build Judge’s stamina for a postseason run in September, which includes potentially playing in games with the Yankees and being pulled before nine innings are complete.

Judge has been working his way back since he was cleared to do baseball activities in August. He was simply hitting off a tee, or getting soft toss, before he could take real batting practice on the field. He was seen in San Diego with the team during their West Coast road trip hitting before games.

JAZZ CHISHOLM JR SAYS KNICKS CHAMPIONSHIP PARADE FUELS HIS WORLD SERIES HUNGER WITH YANKEES

Judge has also been facing a high-velocity pitching machine, while doing outfield and baserunning drills to increase his stamina and get him ready for his role in right field once again.

Either way, the Yankees get back their three-time MVP outfielder and a key cog in their hopes of returning to the World Series.

New York is still four games behind the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays, but they own the top American League Wild Card slot with a nine-game lead heading into Tuesday’s start against the Rockies. At 81-62, the Yankees will be gunning for that top spot in the East, especially considering the winner of it will likely own the top AL playoff spot for the postseason.

The Boston Red Sox are also right behind the Yankees at 80-65 thus far.

Judge was hitting .248/.375/.533 with 17 homers and 38 RBI before hitting the injured list on June 5. The Yankees went 45-38 in the 83 games he’s missed.

While the offense struggled to pick up the slack left by Judge, the pitching staff has been stellar throughout his absence. Thus, Judge’s return couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Yankees, as they hope to match their pitching prowess with more consistent offense during this final regular-season push.

item.title: Ex-MLB southpaw Thomas Pannone dominates for Nashville Sounds with 94-pitch Triple-A perfect game
item.description: Thomas Pannone retired all 27 batters on just 94 pitches for the Nashville Sounds, completing Minor League Baseball's first perfect game since 2017.
item.content:encoded:
Former Major League pitcher Thomas Pannone threw a nine-inning perfect game Monday night, leading the Triple-A Nashville Sounds to a 3-0 win over the Durham Bulls. The 32-year-old southpaw incredibly retired all 27 batters he faced on just 94 pitches.

BREWERS FLAMETHROWER JACOB MISIOROWSKI SETS MLB RECORD FOR PITCHES OVER 100 MPH IN DOMINANT START

Pannone put together an unblemished stat line, racking up nine shutout innings with zero hits, zero walks, and eight strikeouts.

WATCH:

It marks the first nine-inning, single-pitcher perfect game across Minor League Baseball since 2017. It is also just the fifth solo perfect game in the 142-year history of the International League, dating back to 1884.

TREVOR BAUER THROWS NO-HITTER FOR LONG ISLAND DUCKS IN JUST SECOND US START SINCE 2021

The Brewers southpaw pitched with total command, but perfection didn't come without a late dose of drama.

Falling into a tight 3-0 hole against the 27th and final batter in the bottom of the ninth, Pannone faced the immediate risk of a game-ruining walk. Instead, he fired consecutive strikes to battle all the way back, retiring the hitter to lock up the final out.

For this left-hander, flirting with baseball history is nothing new.

During a 49-game run with the Toronto Blue Jays from 2018 to 2019, Pannone carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his Big League debut against Baltimore. In 2019, he threw an immaculate inning against Tampa Bay, striking out the side on nine consecutive pitches.

Since leaving Toronto in 2020, Pannone has taken the classic journeyman route.

Pannone worked through the Cubs, Angels, and Yankees' minor league systems, alongside a pitching stint in the Korean Baseball Organization. He earned a spot start for Milwaukee earlier this summer, marking his first MLB appearance in three years, before returning to Triple-A.

Another shot in the bigs doesn't seem far out of Pannone's future.

item.title: Giants shockingly release longest-tenured player Darius Slayton as John Harbaugh era begins
item.description: Darius Slayton posted a heartfelt farewell after the New York Giants surprisingly cut their longest-tenured player just days before Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
The John Harbaugh era meant change for the New York Giants, but as Week 1 officially got started on Monday, a surprising one came to the 53-man roster.

Wide receiver Darius Slayton, the longest-tenured Giants player entering the 2026 NFL season, was surprisingly released despite initially making the roster out of training camp, the team announced.

Slayton was set to have a cap hit of $15.9 million in 2026, and the Giants save about $3 million in cap space with the move.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Slayton also posted on social media after getting the news from the organization.

"Grateful for my time in NY," he posted on X. "7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what’s next.

JOHN HARBAUGH AND JAXSON DART AIM TO PULL THE NEW YORK GIANTS OUT OF THE NFC EAST BASEMENT

Slayton was a fifth-round draft pick out of Auburn in 2019, where he showed much promise after going for 740 yards on 48 receptions with eight touchdowns. Slayton never became a top receiver option, but he provided depth at the position and continued to make the roster despite multiple coaching changes during his seven-year tenure.

Slayton was never able to find the end zone more than four times in a single season after an eight-touchdown campaign his rookie year, but he may have had more if it weren’t for some costly drops – a pain point amongst the Giants’ fan base when it came to Slayton’s resume.

Heading into this new year, there were questions about Slayton’s job security considering the emergence of several receivers snagged in free agency, let alone another new coaching staff. The Giants brought in Calvin Austin III, Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., which fans loved to see, while also drafting Malachi Fields in the third round.

It was clear Fields was going to make the roster, and though Austin suffered a season-ending injury during training camp, the others were battling for spots.

Fans were delighted to see Beckham make Harbaugh’s squad, as did Mooney. But Slayton had earned the roster spot as well, with Fields and 2024 first-round pick Malik Nabers rounding out the five wideouts in the room.

EX-NFL STAR BELIEVES ODELL BECKHAM JR 'STILL BETTER THAN MOST OF THE RECEIVERS' IN NFL AS HE RETURNS TO GIANTS

With Slayton’s release, it could indicate that Nabers is indeed ready for Week 1, which is where he was trending after surprising many with how he was moving at practice throughout the last month. Still, the Giants haven’t made it a definite that their first-rounder and top wide receiver will be on the field for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys.

If he isn’t, that leaves Mooney, Fields and Beckham to take over the workload out wide for quarterback Jaxson Dart.

Meanwhile, Slayton could find a new home elsewhere for those who are not as happy with their receiver depth entering the new season.

item.title: US forces sink narco-refueling station linked to Ecuadorian cartel in Pacific: SOUTHCOM
item.description: U.S. forces sank a Los Choneros refueling vessel in the Eastern Pacific after SOUTHCOM said it supported at-sea drug trafficking operations.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. forces on Monday sank a floating refueling vessel used by an Ecuadorian organized crime ring, officials said.

Forces with Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTFWH) interdicted the refueling vessel used for "at-sea drug trafficking operations" in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said.

"JTF-WHEM continues to conduct precise and professional operations to dismantle the logistical networks fueling narco-trafficking in the Western Hemisphere," a SOUTHCOM post on X states.

The vessel was involved with the Los Choneros narco-terrorist organization, SOUTHCOM said. The people aboard were removed and will be handed over to Ecuadorian authorities.

NEWLY UNCLASSIFIED PENTAGON IMAGES SHOW SUSPECTED DRUG BOATS AS OFFICIAL ISSUES DEADLY WARNING

Once the boat was cleared, U.S. forces sank it.

JTFWH was activated by SOUTHCOM in August to counter threats, strengthen regional security, and respond to crises in the Western Hemisphere.

The Trump administration has prioritized targeting suspected drug-smuggling vessels bound for the United States.

US KILLS TWO 'NARCO-TERRORISTS' IN STRIKE 2 MONTHS SINCE LAST ANNOUNCED ANTI-'NARCO-TRAFFICKING' ATTACK

U.S. forces have launched dozens of strikes targeting such boats under the administration's anti-drug campaign.

Last week, the cartel was designated by the State Department as a foreign terrorist organization. Its members have attacked and threatened public officials and their families, security personnel, judges, prosecutors, and journalists in Ecuador, the agency said.

"Their ultimate goal is to control drug trafficking routes through Ecuador by terrorizing and inflicting brutal violence on the Ecuadorian people," said State Department deputy spokesperson Thomas Pigott.

In July, U.S. and Ecuadorian authorities cooperated to extradite Los Choneros leader Fito Macias, who was the first Ecuadorian citizen extradited from Ecuador to face justice in the U.S.

item.title: Julia Louis-Dreyfus reveals ‘tons’ of friction behind the scenes of ‘Seinfeld’
item.description: Julia Louis-Dreyfus opened up on the "Friends Keep Secrets" podcast about the arguments and hard work that shaped "Seinfeld" into a phenomenon.
item.content:encoded:
Julia Louis-Dreyfus didn't mince words about what it took to make "Seinfeld" a television phenomenon.

The actress, who starred as Elaine Benes, revealed there was "tons" of friction behind the scenes as the cast and creators worked to get the groundbreaking comedy just right.

"Well, I mean, it's hard to do anything really well, and it takes a lot of work, and you're gonna butt heads," she explained during an appearance on the "Friends Keep Secrets" podcast.

According to Louis-Dreyfus, creators Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld were "collaborative" with the cast when it came to direction. However, "sometimes there was an argument."

RECLUSIVE 'SEINFELD' STAR MICHAEL RICHARDS MAKES RARE PUBLIC APPEARANCE AFTER TWO-YEAR ABSENCE FROM SPOTLIGHT

Despite the occasional clashes, Louis-Dreyfus believed in what they were creating from the start. Her bigger concern was whether NBC would see the same potential.

"I thought it was, I thought it was really good," she noted. "Those first four. I thought, ‘Wow, this is so unusual.’ And then I thought, 'The network is too stupid. They'll never pick it up.'"

The actress recalled filming the comedy hit alongside Seinfeld, Jason Alexander and Michael Richards as "just being friends together and just hanging out."

"That sounds as if it was just hanging out. It was a lot of work to make the show," she clarified.

"Seinfeld" aired on NBC from 1989 until 1998. Set largely in New York City, the series follows a fictionalized version of comedian Jerry Seinfeld and his close-knit, frequently self-absorbed circle of friends: George Costanza, Elaine Benes and Cosmo Kramer.

Often described as a "show about nothing," "Seinfeld" built its comedy around the small annoyances, unwritten social rules and awkward encounters of everyday life.

"Seinfeld" ran for nine seasons and 180 episodes and won the 1993 Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series. Its May 1998 series finale became a major television event, drawing an estimated 76 million U.S. viewers. 

Decades later, the show remains influential for its unconventional storytelling, interconnected plots, catchphrases and willingness to make its principal characters funny without necessarily making them likable.

item.title: Christine Taylor was asked to lose 10 pounds after landing Marcia Brady role in 'Brady Bunch Movie'
item.description: Christine Taylor revealed she was asked to lose 10 pounds for her role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie" during the "Office Ladies" podcast.
item.content:encoded:
Christine Taylor landed her dream role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie" – but the part came with a catch.

The "Brady Bunch Movie" star recalled the uncomfortable demand she received after landing the role of Marcia Brady during the "Office Ladies" podcast, revealing she was "embarrassed" but agreed to do it because "that was just how things went" in Hollywood at the time.

Taylor landed the role of Marcia after starring in a live show called "The Real Live Brady Bunch."

 The actress had been obsessed with Marcia Brady for years and had seen "every single episode ... backwards and forwards, inside out."

MICHELLE PFEIFFER SAYS SHE FELT 'HUMILIATED' FOLLOWING HER AUDITION FOR HER BREAKTHROUGH ROLE IN 'GREASE 2'

"And then out-of-the-blue one day, I mean, out of the blue on my answering machine in 1990, whatever year this was, 92 or 93, I got a message from Sherwood Schwartz calling me, just cold calling me saying, 'I would love to meet with you...'" she recalled.

For Taylor, getting a personal call from "The Brady Bunch" creator was the kind of Hollywood moment she never expected – and one she wished she had preserved.

"It was a pinch me moment that I cannot believe to this day that I still didn't keep my little tape from the answering machine," she added.

But beneath the disbelief, Taylor said she had no doubts about whether she was right for the role.

‘BRADY BUNCH’ STAR SHARES THE SIMPLE WORD THAT SAVED HER FROM HOLLYWOOD TRAPS

"I knew it in my core that there was nobody who could do it better than me," Taylor remembered.

That confidence appeared to carry her through the casting process, which Taylor remembered as surprisingly straightforward.

"I'm fairly sure that I met with them and that was pretty much it," she recalled. "They didn't tell me I got it, but I never had to go back in and audition solo again."

Instead, Taylor read with different actors who would later portray her siblings – Jan and Cindy.

But Taylor said the role also came with a request that reflected a much different era in Hollywood."...It was a very different time in the industry," Taylor explained of the 90s era. "The one thing that I got, and I was not a super heavy person, but they asked me to lose 10 pounds."

Taylor emphasized that she wasn't heavy at the time, but said dropping the weight felt like just another requirement of getting the job.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I was like, 'I'll lose 10 pounds,'" she admitted. "Of course I was embarrassed when that ask came my way because, by the way, it would never happen today. And also it just was like, I wasn't the only person ever being asked to lose weight for a role back then. That was just how things went."

"But I was like, 'I'll do it.' And then the joke is over the course of the movie, which if you watch it very closely, I start to put the 10 pounds back on, and you can see it," Taylor recalled. Like I'll come into a scene looking a little rounder. And then like I exit the scene looking a little thinner just because of how they had to reshoot things."

Whatever pressure Taylor felt to shed weight didn't stop her from enjoying herself once the cameras stopped rolling.

"But no, over the course of the movie, I really started to treat myself," she explained. "Nonfat frozen yogurt was the big craze at the time. And that was my treat. I was like, 'Oh, I wrapped. I'm going to meet my roommate. We're going to go to the Big Chill and get a frozen yogurt with a huge thing of sprinkles on the side.'"

item.title: Jimmy John's employee accused of opening fire on car, shooting 14-year-old girl in leg: police
item.description: Police say that a dispute at a St. Louis Jimmy John's escalated into gunfire, leaving a 14-year-old girl wounded and an employee facing felony charges.
item.content:encoded:
A dispute that began at a Jimmy John's restaurant in St. Louis ended with a 14-year-old girl shot in the leg and a restaurant employee facing charges for allegedly opening fire on a vehicle carrying the teen, according to police and court records.

The teenage girl was struck shortly before 6 p.m. Saturday near the intersection of Vandeventer and Laclede avenues and was taken to a local hospital, where she was listed in stable condition, the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department said in a statement on X.

Court documents identified the alleged shooter as 27-year-old Adam White, whom police say was an employee at the Jimmy John's where the confrontation began.

MISSOURI ASSISTANT FIRE CHIEF CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER HIDDEN VIDEO FOUND ON WIFE'S PHONE, INVESTIGATORS SAY

White is charged with first-degree assault, armed criminal action, unlawful use of a weapon, first-degree child endangerment, among other felony offenses. 

In their statement, police said the shooting stemmed from a dispute involving the teenage girl's mother and "several individuals" associated with the Jimmy John's in the 3800 block of Laclede.

"A preliminary investigation indicates the shooting followed a disagreement involving the girl’s mother and several individuals associated with the Jimmy John’s in the 3800 block of Laclede. The mother’s connection to the restaurant remains under investigation," the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department said.

According to investigators, the girl's mother's boyfriend later arrived at the restaurant with the 14-year-old. The confrontation escalated, and gunfire erupted.

GOP CANDIDATE GETS BUSTED ALLEGEDLY TRYING TO PLANT DRUGS ON HIS POLITICAL RIVAL

Court documents allege that White got into a verbal argument with a former employee, which continued into the parking lot. 

Police say the former employee, her boyfriend and her juvenile daughter then got into a vehicle.

As the vehicle drove away, White allegedly fired multiple rounds into its rear, striking the teenage girl in the left leg.

"As they drove off, the defendant fired multiple rounds into the rear of the vehicle. Victim 3, the juvenile, was struck by one of the bullets in her left leg," court documents state.

Investigators said they found ballistic damage to the trunk of the vehicle.

US MARSHALS SURVIVE DECK COLLAPSE WHILE SERVING WARRANT AT SEX OFFENDER'S HOME

According to court documents, White initially fled the scene but later returned and was taken into custody. After being advised of his Miranda rights, White allegedly admitted firing at the vehicle and told detectives he had left the gun at his home.

A judge ordered White held without bond pending trial.

Jimmy John's and the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: SEC teams went 16-0 in Week 1, is the conference back on top of college football world?
item.description: The SEC went 16-0 in week one, but after three straight Big Ten national championships, do the results really shift the college football hierarchy?
item.content:encoded:
After three straight national championship wins, few would argue that the Big Ten has become the top conference in college football. Three years, three different teams, including a 16-0 season from the Indiana Hoosiers that coaches like Texas' Steve Sarkisian believed were essentially impossible in the modern era.

Entering the 2026 season, most believed that the Big Ten would once again be the cream of the college football crop, thanks to Ohio State and Oregon topping the country in most human, and computer, ranking systems.

But fast forward through week one's results, and there's one, very familiar, conference tooting its own horn about where it ranks in the college football hierarchy: the SEC.

HAS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP PICTURE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL ALREADY CHANGED AFTER A STUNNING FIRST WEEK?

The SEC through week one went 16-0, an impressive feat for any conference, and an indication that their impressive depth will once again be relevant in 2026. Some fans have been quick to suggest that this means the SEC is back on top, that the Playoff and national championship will once again run through the previously dominant conference. But how much can we learn about where the SEC sits? Or at least, where these individual teams sit in the season-long picture?

Well, a little, and also, not very much. Let's take a quick look at how the SEC got to 16-0 and what it all means.

Missouri was the first win of the weekend, with a 56-14 drubbing of Arkansas Pine-Bluff. Nothing to glean from that. On Friday, Oklahoma shut out UTEP 51-0. The Miners were 127th out of 138 FBS teams in SP+ heading into the season, but still, the Sooners did what they needed to do against a bad team.

Alabama handled East Carolina, South Carolina throttled Kent State, Kentucky beat up on Youngstown State, Georgia predictably beat down Tennessee State, Tennessee won 56-9 over Furman, Texas took care of Texas State, Texas A&M shut out Missouri State, and Mississippi State won 62-13 over UL Monroe. Despite giving up 14 first half points to Florida Atlantic, the Gators cruised 66-21. Arkansas was unimpressive in a 31-14 win over FCS North Alabama, and Vanderbilt stretched a 15-9 halftime lead over Austin Peay into a 28-9 win.

LSU'S LANE KIFFIN ADMITS HE LET TIGER STADIUM WEATHER DELAY DRAG ON IN ORDER TO HURT CLEMSON

All better than Rutgers' performance, without question. But these were all games that the SEC team should win easily, and they did.

The three other games, LSU-Clemson, Ole Miss-Louisville, and Auburn-Baylor, said a bit more about where the conference sits. LSU, of course, dismantled and humiliated Clemson, and immediately made a strong case as a conference challenger alongside Texas, Georgia, and Alabama. Auburn was favored by 6.5 points, but the game turned out to be evenly matched.

After a back-and-forth battle, Baylor went for the aggressive play to win in regulation instead of sending the game to overtime, only to come up inches short of a two-point conversion to take an 18-17 lead. An evenly matched game between two evenly matched teams that doesn't tell us much about which team is "better," necessarily, particularly given Auburn's unimpressive performance against the spread. Baylor after all, was No. 54 in preseason SP+, while Auburn was No. 26. They should have won, and they did, but without answering questions about their prognosis for the rest of the season.

Similarly, Ole Miss should have handled Louisville. They were favored by 6.5 points, came into the season 11 places ahead of Louisville in SP+, and won on a walk-off field goal. Louisville, if anything, slightly outplayed the Rebels, racking up 6.9 yards per play to 6.3 for Ole Miss. They were better at protecting the ball and had a higher average yards per carry, while adding 10.6 yards per attempt passing.

GREG SANKEY INSISTS SEC IS 'STRONGEST LEAGUE' DESPITE BIG TEN WINNING THREE STRAIGHT NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIPS

Ole Miss gets credit for the win, as they should, but again, they were favored, should have won, and were fortunate to do so.

Which is where this all shakes out. In the three games against other Power 4 schools, the SEC team was favored by 6.5, 6.5, and 10 points. In two of those games, they failed to cover and won what amounts to a toss-up. In the other? Well, let's just say LSU set the Clemson program back years.

There's no question going 16-0 is great, impressive, and signals that the SEC is far from in decline. They also were "supposed" to go 16-0. That's easier said than done, sure, but it's hardly a shock that three games in which they were favored went in their direction. Especially two toss-ups, which could have gone either way.

The Big Ten, by contrast, was generally far less impressive. Rutgers, obviously, lost in humiliating fashion to UMass. Oregon struggled to put away Boise State, Michigan "escaped" against Western Michigan, and Wisconsin couldn't keep up with Notre Dame in the second half.

But we've seen, time and time again, that week one can be deceiving. USC in 2024 beat LSU in the season opener and moved up into the top 15, only to finish 6-6 in the regular season. Indiana beat Old Dominion 27-14 in week one, then beat Ohio State, Penn State, Oregon, Alabama, Oregon again, and Miami on their way to winning a title.

Week 1 matters, but it's not definitive.

item.title: Georgetown students plan Charlie Kirk 'lookalike contest' on anniversary of his assassination
item.description: Georgetown University students promoted a Charlie Kirk lookalike contest on Fizz, the anonymous social media app, drawing over 2,200 upvotes on campus.
item.content:encoded:
Students at Georgetown University are allegedly planning a Charlie Kirk "lookalike contest" for the anniversary of the conservative activist’s assassination, with the event drawing thousands of upvotes at the elite Washington, D.C., campus, according to screenshots shared with Fox News Digital from the school’s Turning Point USA chapter.

The Sept. 10 event was promoted on Fizz, an anonymous social media platform popular with Georgetown students, where the initial announcement received more than 2,200 upvotes. Georgetown's undergraduate population is roughly 6,000.

The post that received 2,200 upvotes read, "Charlie Kirk lookalike contest. September 10th 2026. Pull up to Copley Lawn to speak the truth while the cost is high."

INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES

Georgetown's TPUSA chapter said members believe the slogan "pull up to Copley Lawn and speak the truth while the cost is high" is likely a mocking statement.

Copley Lawn is an area right outside the school's most iconic landmark, Healy Hall, which resembles a castle.

The Turning Point USA chapter responded by setting up a table on campus with American flags, stickers and signs condemning the planned event, according to the group.

TEXAS MAN ALLEGEDLY THREATENED TO BOMB TURNING POINT USA EVENT AND KILL CEO ERIKA KIRK IN ONLINE POSTS

According to posts on the Fizz app, there has also been an Erika Kirk look-alike contest discussed, with someone commenting, "Can the winner of the Charlie Kirk one be prom king with the winner of this?"

The group says that they are not sure who started the calls for the lookalike contest, but believe it was first brought up on Fizz, which they say is the most popular anonymous platform used by Georgetown students. According to the group, users must be affiliated with Georgetown University in order to log into Georgetown's Fizz as it requires a "@georgetown.edu" email address.

One Fizz user appeared to suggest The Georgetown Chimes, a choral group at the school, sing a Charlie Kirk meme song, "We Are Charlie Kirk" writing, "Any chance Gtown Chimes could learn this before Thursday?"

HASAN PIKER SINGS MOCKING 'WE ARE CHARLIE KIRK' SONG AT LIVE PODCAST SHOW

The song, thought to be AI-generated, was released shortly after Kirk's assassination in Utah.

Another post, shared on the Georgetown Fizz account, read, "Happy Kirkiversary, September 10th, on Healy Lawn," and included what appeared to be an AI-generated image of Kirk, and included the phrases, 
"Georgetown University," "Honoring leadership, inspiring truth," and "Charlie Kirk lookalike contest."

JONATHAN TURLEY: PIKER'S CHARLIE KIRK ATTACK SHOWS HE IS HATEFUL LEFT'S PIED PIPER

Heidi Sui, Turning Point USA's Georgetown University Chapter President, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "The TPUSA Chapter at Georgetown strongly condemns any events that aim to disrespect Charlie Kirk and the upcoming memorial ceremony at UVU.

These events are not representative of how Americans feel about Charlie and his legacy. To the millions of us who listened to his debates, Charlie never celebrated violence. But some liberal students do. And they are doing it right here — in our nation’s capital of all places.

This reaction from Georgetown students should disturb us regardless of our political affiliation. There is a difference between disagreeing with someone’s politics and celebrating their death."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Andrew Kolvet, TPUSA's spokesman said, "A culture that can no longer simply mourn the fallen, or respect them enough to at least keep their mouth shut, is a culture that has lost touch with a basic sense of shared humanity. Shame on any of the mockers and trolls who debase themselves by continuously proving Charlie outclassed them in every conceivable way."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a Georgetown University spokesperson said, "We have seen no activity on campus related to these posts. Georgetown is not planning such an event and, to our knowledge, no student organization is hosting or planning such an event. We take these anonymous posts seriously and condemn their language as deeply inconsistent with Georgetown University’s values. We are monitoring this closely to ensure the safety of the University community."

The spokesperson continued, "Georgetown is committed to ensuring that all members of our community have a safe and welcoming place to learn and receive the support they need to do so. We seek to create a living and learning community that promotes thoughtful, respectful dialogue."

The spokesperson added, "While Georgetown’s policies give latitude for the free expression of ideas and opinions, making light of a victim of violence is counter to our values and deeply disappointing. Students are expected to know the policies that guide life on campus, including the Speech and Expression policy and the Code of Student Conduct."

item.title: Fans disagree with Portland Thorns over reason for ejection in XX-XY apparel dispute: 'They are lying'
item.description: Video shows Portland Thorns fans removed from Providence Park over women's sports apparel, with Amy Sousa denying claims of distributing materials.
item.content:encoded:
A Portland Thorns spokesperson said eight fans were removed from Providence Park during the NWSL club’s Sept. 6 match against the Washington Spirit for distributing "unapproved materials," a claim the group disputes.

In a statement sent to OutKick, the Thorns spokesperson said, "During our September 6 match against the Washington Spirit, individuals were removed from Providence Park for distributing unapproved materials, a violation of the Fan Experience Guidelines at the stadium. Our priority remains fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment for every fan at Providence Park." The Thorns spokesperson added that the matter is still being investigated.

Amy Sousa, who was part of the group, denied the allegation, saying the fans were targeted for political reasons and were expressing support for women’s sports.

WNBA FACES GROWING SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM MOVEMENT AS NEW RALLIES ARE SET FOR FEVER GAMES IN OREGON, MINNESOTA

"We did not distribute any materials. We came armed with copies of their own code of conduct and we followed it to the letter," Sousa said in a statement sent to OutKick. "They are lying about us. They have violated our rights. My group was targeted for political beliefs I speak about online."

The group was wearing XX-XY Athletics apparel and shirts bearing messages including "Save Women’s Sports," "Girls just wanna have fundamental rights," "Woman" and "It’s common sense."

Video showed Sousa questioning her removal after she had entered the stadium and taken her seat. Security handed the group of eight a Providence Park notice and escorted them out after a dispute over whether they were distributing materials, a claim Sousa denies.

The notice cited a Code of Conduct violation and warned of additional penalties, including a possible ban.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS OPEN UP ON ENCOUNTER WITH SECURITY, PRO-TRANS FANS IN LATEST WNBA CULTURE CLASH

Ahead of the match, Sousa said she brought five printed copies of the NWSL and Providence Park codes of conduct after receiving a message from local activist Hannah Perry.

Sousa said Perry had warned her that she was contacting officials about the group’s planned attendance, so she wanted to be prepared to reference the venue’s rules. Sousa also said the group only shared the printed copies among themselves while seated.

WNBA ADMITS SECURITY IN ATLANTA WAS WRONG TO MAKE FANS COVER SHIRTS AT DREAM-FEVER GAME

"We only shared them to our own group while seated facing each other. We only brought five," she said. "If we ‘distributed’ anything, they would have it on video."

Sousa also said the group’s XX-XY clothing was covered when they initially entered the stadium.

MOM AND DAUGHTER TOLD TO COVER UP XX-XY T-SHIRTS, SAY THEY WERE THREATENED WITH EJECTION AT FEVER-DREAM GAME

"And our XX/XY Clothes were not visible when we arrived," Sousa said.

The dispute continued after the group left Providence Park.

After leaving, the group went to The Sports Bra, a Portland bar focused on women’s sports. Members were later asked to leave.

Video from inside the bar showed a staff member ordering the group to leave after accusing them of wearing "transphobic" clothing.

The Sports Bra later released a statement on social media defending its decision.

"At The Sports Bra, our mission is simple: support, promote, and empower ALL girls and women in sports," the bar said. "To be clear: trans girls are girls, and trans women are women."

The statement added that while it welcomes people of every identity and background, it does "not tolerate messages or conduct that demean or exclude the very community we exist to serve and celebrate."

"On Sunday, Sept. 6, a group entered wearing apparel with messages advocating for the exclusion of trans women from sports," the statement continued. "When our team respectfully gave the group notice to cover the anti-trans messaging or leave, they chose to leave."

The fallout continues as women’s sports organizations promote their cultural messaging to paying fans and show the door to those who refuse to fall in line.

item.title: Prosecutors drop Khalid Sheikh Mohammed confession appeal to protect 2028 trial for alleged 9/11 mastermind
item.description: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed's 2007 confession was thrown out over "severe coercion," but prosecutors won't appeal to protect the June 2028 trial date.
item.content:encoded:
Military prosecutors will move ahead with the trial against the mastermind of the Sept. 11 attacks without a key confession, a decision made to avoid further delays in the long-awaited proceedings scheduled for 2028.

The federal government has decided not to appeal a recent ruling by a military judge that threw out statements made by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed in 2007. 

The decision means Mohammed's statements to the FBI cannot be used at trial.

"An appeal could jeopardize the hard-earned June 5, 2028, trial date," the prosecution team's liaison to victims wrote in a letter Friday — a week before the 25th anniversary of the attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people, sources familiar with the matter told The New York Post.

NEW EVIDENCE IN LOCKERBIE PAN AM FLIGHT 103 BOMBING CASE PUSHES FEDERAL JUDGE TO POSTPONE TRIAL

Appeals can take years to resolve, an outcome military prosecutors want to avoid given the series of delays that have prolonged the wait for victims' families to receive justice. Mohammed and his alleged co-conspirators — Walid bin Attash, Mustafa al-Hawsawi, and Ammar al-Baluchi — are scheduled to go on trial in June 2028.

Prosecutors initially planned to use a confession obtained from Mohammed at Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, where he has been held for nearly two decades.

9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

Lt. Col. Michael Schrama set the trial date last month before suppressing the confession. He cited "severe coercion" and noted that Mohammed did not have an opportunity to consult with an attorney.

Mohammed and two of his co-defendants had agreed to a plea deal with the Biden administration in 2024 that would have spared them the death penalty.

The deal was subsequently revoked following public outcry, resulting in further lengthy litigation.

Meanwhile, 9/11 families have asked the Trump administration to declassify documents on Saudi Arabia's alleged role in the attacks.

item.title: NTSB reveals if crew survived Amazon cargo jet disaster as it shares details about victims
item.description: The NTSB said the crew survived after the Amazon cargo plane overran the runway, caught fire and collided with two vehicles carrying eight occupants.
item.content:encoded:
Federal regulators said the two crew members aboard the Amazon cargo jet that crashed at Miami International Airport on Sunday survived the accident.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) provided the update during a Sunday press conference after officials said the cargo plane overran the runway and caught fire while landing. The crash killed five people and injured five others, authorities said Sunday. 

The jet collided with two vehicles carrying at least eight occupants, according to NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy. 

Seven of the victims were in a van that was struck and "torn apart" on airport grounds, Homendy said. The 2012 white Ford Econoline van was owned by Ocean Service Corporation, a contract cleaning company that provides services for airlines, she said. 

AMAZON CARGO PLANE OVERRUNS MIAMI AIRPORT RUNWAY AND STRIKES 'MULTIPLE' VEHICLES; 5 DEAD, 5 INJURED

The NTSB said the aircraft then crashed through the airport perimeter and struck a civilian vehicle, a Toyota Corolla Cross LE, that was traveling on Northwest 67th Avenue. 

Homendy said investigators observed what appeared to be deployed airbags in the vehicles as they surveyed the crash site. 

"You can see components from vehicles, both passenger vehicles and the aircraft itself," Homendy said. 

The jet then "continued into the grass and impacted another fence line, which separated an area where Tesla robotaxis were stationed," Homendy said. 

In total, the jet reportedly traveled 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface. 

Homendy said the wreckage was "extensive," noting that the crash damaged airport navigational aids and equipment, while fencing was ripped apart throughout the area.  

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Officials said the Boeing 767 had completed two other flights before crashing in Miami, where its operator, 21 Air LLC, is based. 

The aircraft traveled from Cincinnati to Miami, then from Miami to San Juan, Puerto Rico, before returning to Miami, Homendy said. 

NTSB investigators have recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder, which they planned to examine. 

Homendy described the crash site as "devastating," saying wreckage was scattered throughout the area. 

"I would describe it in one word, devastating, utter devastation," she said.

"I mean, you can see on the paved surface, tire marks that continue through the grass. There's debris everywhere."

item.title: Russia’s quieter nuclear submarines threaten NATO, former commander warns
item.description: Russia's Yasen-M submarines and militarized Kola Peninsula are forcing NATO to confront a growing undersea threat across the GIUK Gap and Arctic, expert warns.
item.content:encoded:
Russia’s quieter new-generation nuclear-powered submarines are pressuring NATO’s northern defenses as the alliance races to secure Arctic and North Atlantic approaches to North America, a former NATO commander warned, citing President Vladimir Putin’s emerging "new super weapons and super capabilities" amassing in the region.

The rising challenge, he said, also includes Russia’s heavily militarized Kola Peninsula, where Moscow has expanded military infrastructure, including airfields and ports, as it seeks to strengthen its position along the Northern Sea Route, as well as the waters leading to the Greenland-Iceland-United Kingdom Gap, known as the GIUK Gap.

NATO’s Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum highlighted Sept. 2 that an expanding Russian submarine threat in the region was "serious."

"Something is moving beneath the surface," NATO Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum posted on X.

ARCTIC POWER PLAY GIVES TOP US ADVERSARY NEW OPENING WITH RUSSIA AS US STAKES GROW

"Russia is expanding and modernising its submarine force, with the Kola Peninsula remaining a key hub for the Northern Fleet. Among them: new-generation nuclear-powered SSGNs, bringing serious long-range strike and sea-denial capabilities into the High North," NATO Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum said.

"They may be invisible beneath the waves. But not for us. We see them, we watch the developments closely and yes, we take these developments seriously," the Joint Force Command added.

The combination of quieter nuclear submarines and Russia's growing military infrastructure across its Arctic coastline means NATO is confronting an increasingly difficult undersea surveillance challenge, retired Gen. Philip Breedlove told Fox News Digital.

"Submarines are one of the toughest threats that we have to deal with — they're very hard to find and track," he explained.

"Submarines can get well within striking distance of any nation in the Atlantic. From the United States to our NATO allies, submarines can get close enough to the shore to fire submarine-launched ballistic missiles and cruise missiles, which are a major problem," the former supreme allied commander Europe for NATO and commander of U.S. European Command added. 

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

Today, countries such as Russia and China are developing similar fleets, posing a growing threat to any nation with a significant coastline, Breedlove said.

"We've taken very capable measures in the past to understand what Russia is doing in those waters, and we will now be adapting to the possibility of a quieter submarine," he said. "Any increase in stealthiness or noise suppression by a Russian submarine is, of course, a problem for NATO."

Russia's Yasen-M-class nuclear-powered submarines include advanced acoustic-quieting and sonar technology, according to Military Watch and Russian news agency, TASS.

According to the U.S. Naval Institute, the 13,800-ton submarines can carry 1,000-mile-range cruise missiles, anti-ship missiles and hypersonic anti-ship cruise missiles, with Russian officials stating they remain "invisible."

"Yasen-M-class nuclear-powered submarines are capable of accomplishing all of the Navy’s objectives in any part of the World Ocean while remaining invisible," Russian Navy Commander-in-Chief Fleet Adm. Alexander Moiseyev said in a June 17 statement, according to TASS, after Russia's Sevmash shipyard started building the ninth Yasen-M submarine.

NATO'S EASTERN FLANK RACES TO REARM AS TRUMP PRESSURE EXPOSES WESTERN EUROPE'S DEFENSE GAP

"As is often the case when Putin is in trouble — and he's in trouble now in his war in Ukraine — one of the ways he diverts attention is to start announcing new super weapons and super capabilities that NATO and the West can't contend with," Breedlove warned.

"Putin is creating a stir about a new class of submarines that he wants to deploy from what we call the bastion waters in the Far North," he said before stating that NATO would "have to adapt our measures and our ability to see and track them."

"We've taken excellent measures in the past." 

Breedlove characterized the GIUK Gap as a critical gateway for Russian naval forces moving from their northern bases toward the Atlantic.

"All the Russian ships have to come out through the GIUK Gap to make it into the Atlantic," Breedlove said, warning that the seven other Arctic nations, including the United States, are concerned about what Russia is doing.

A UKRAINIAN HACKER'S TALE OF HOW HE IS AIDING THE LAND WAR BY BATTLING RUSSIA FOR THE CLOUD

NATO has also been strengthening its northern posture amid the renewed Russian military activity and the growing strategic importance of the Arctic.

In February 2026, the alliance launched Arctic Sentry, a multidomain military initiative led by Joint Force Command Norfolk and designed to better coordinate allied land, air and maritime activity across the Arctic and High North.

NATO further strengthened its northern flank in June with Forward Land Forces Finland, a Swedish-led multinational force designed to bolster deterrence and defense along the alliance's northeastern flank, with Finland serving as the host nation, according to a release.

"The Arctic region has been a concern for some years now as ice in the area is receding in the north, and what that has done is created the Northern Passage that allows European trade to happen with Asia much faster," Breedlove said, stating that for most types of ships, the trips are up to 14 days quicker.

"This is a tremendous economic opportunity, but Russia sees this as an economic opportunity in that they want to control those northern waters.

DENMARK VOWS TO DEFEND GREENLAND AFTER TRUMP REITERATES US SHOULD CONTROL TERRITORY

Russia has been upgrading airfields, ports and radar systems along the Arctic coast as Moscow seeks greater control over the Northern Sea Route and its commercial traffic, Breedlove said.

The recent NATO buildup however, has drawn strong pushback from Moscow, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov warning Aug. 30 that increased Western military activity risks destabilizing the Arctic region.

"Such military activity in the Far North poses a direct threat to Russia’s security," Lavrov wrote in a public essay.

"It also increases the risk of incidents that could trigger an armed confrontation with potentially disastrous consequences," he said, according to Reuters.

item.title: LSU's Lane Kiffin admits he let Tiger Stadium weather delay drag on in order to hurt Clemson
item.description: The LSU Tigers racked up 644 total yards and 10 tackles for loss in Lane Kiffin's dominant debut, cementing themselves as a playoff contender.
item.content:encoded:
Perhaps the most impressive performance of a wild week one in college football was the LSU Tigers' complete demolition of a once-proud Clemson program.

The final score, 51-10, is somehow representative, and yet not sufficient to demonstrate how dominant the Tigers were in Lane Kiffin's LSU debut. Under new quarterback Sam Leavitt and a revamped, transfer-heavy roster, they racked up a remarkable 644 yards on offense, including 309 rushing yards on 58 attempts.

They were equally stifling on defense, giving up just 40 rushing yards on 26 attempts and an anemic 3.0 yards per play, including yardage allowed in garbage time well after the game was decided. To call their defenders "swarming" would be an understatement. Though Clemson rarely had possession, the LSU defense racked up an astonishing 10 tackles for loss and four sacks.

LSU HAD A REVIVAL, CLEMSON WAS AT A FUNERAL: LANE KIFFIN’S DEBUT SENDS A LOUD MESSAGE TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL

It was a dismantling. An embarrassment for Clemson. A statement win for LSU that immediately cemented the Tigers as a College Football Playoff contender, even with a tough schedule. And as Kiffin himself joked, they didn't even need their NFL players on the field to do it.

LIVVY DUNNE AND BROOKS NADER JOIN LANE'S FIRST TIGER WALK, TRICIA WHITAKER WANTS INDIANA REPEAT & TONS OF MEAT

That commitment to finding every advantage, no matter how small, has become a hallmark of Kiffin's strategy with roster construction and in-game management. And he admitted he brought that mentality to, of all of things, the weather delay in Baton Rouge ahead of kickoff.

That weather delay lasted for nearly two hours, with a 90-minute warm up period after lightning was spotted within eight miles of the stadium. And he told reporters after the win that he declined, purposefully, to make Clemson suffer in the terrible Tiger Stadium visiting locker room.

"That locker room sucks over there," he said afterwards. "And when you sit in there, the longer you sit in there – No, it's a real thing."

"If you haven't figured out my competitiveness in order to win, if I'm gonna go through all that other stuff for two players, nationally, I'm certainly gonna," he added. "If I think 90 minutes is gonna help us win the game, we're gonna sit in the locker room for 90 minutes."

Is that the reason LSU won? No, of course not. But it is indicative of the mentality Kiffin has brought to Baton Rouge, for good and in the case of the pro player debacle, bad. Find every advantage, turn over every rock, look for every opportunity to make the Tigers better, and put opponents on the back foot.

item.title: Indiana farm vows to ‘absolutely’ do Charlie Kirk corn maze again despite wave of backlash
item.description: Global Farms says critics flooded its Google reviews with one-star ratings after unveiling the Charlie Kirk corn maze, but worldwide support followed.
item.content:encoded:
An Indiana family farm facing backlash over a massive corn maze honoring Charlie Kirk says it has no regrets about the tribute and would "absolutely" do it again, telling Fox News Digital that critics began hammering the business with one-star reviews almost immediately after the design was unveiled.

Jeremy Goebel, a manager at family-owned Global Farms, said the farm never intended for the maze to be divisive, but wanted to remember Kirk and his advocacy for open debate and free speech.

"Absolutely, we would absolutely do it again," Goebel said. "And although, you know, this is just pushback and negative commentary on us, I don't really feel like it's directed at us. I mean, sure, people are saying. It's about us, but it's really about Charlie. They have the issue with what he stood for."

HOW CHARLIE KIRK INSPIRED HIS MENTOR'S FIGHT TO DEFEND REALITY

The Turning Point USA president was assassinated Sept. 10, 2025, while speaking at Utah Valley University during his "American Comeback Tour."

Goebel said the backlash began the same day the farm announced the maze, with some people, including previous customers, leaving one-star reviews because they opposed the tribute.

BUFFALO MUSIC VENUE BANS DJ AFTER 'WE ARE CHARLIE KIRK' SONG PLAYED IN JEST

"Unfortunately, the first day that we had announced it, people began giving us one-star reviews, even some previous customers, because they posted their photos with their one-star review, simply because they disagreed with the corn maze," Goebel said. "And so we got a message from Google saying that someone had said that we were doing deceptive practices, and so they closed the profile, at least temporarily until we have a chance to appeal it."

For Goebel, the backlash has been hard to understand.

HE FLED COMMUNISM. NOW THIS CALIFORNIA MAYOR IS HONORING CHARLIE KIRK AND REFUSING TO BACK DOWN

"I just think it's very hard to wrap my mind around the fact that there's been so much hate over this, we were just trying to remember a man who lost his life promoting freedom of speech," Goebel said. "I know not everybody agrees with him, and I'm not saying that we agreed with everything, and I'm not saying that we disagreed with everything, but, we just wanted to remember someone who lost their life for the cause of free speech and to get people educated."

But the response has not been all negative, Goebel said.

ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION

"We've received a lot of backlash over the last few days, but especially that first day, the last 24 hours, I would say the majority is positive, actually," Goebel said. "Actually, I've heard from people all over the world, from Cape Town, South Africa, and even Australia, actually, in support of it. So I think it was never intended to be divisive. It was only just to remember Charlie, because obviously he lost his life."

He said the country would do better to listen more to each other.

"I think part of what makes America great is that we can challenge each other’s ideas and disagree," Goebel told Fox News Digital. "No one side has all the answers, and I think a lot of our best ideas and progress come from people with different perspectives pushing each other to think differently. We probably accomplish more as a society when we’re willing to listen to each other instead of just assuming the other side is wrong."
