item.title: Outraged cruise passengers sound off about 'immense disappointment' after abrupt cancellation
item.description: Serenade of the Seas by Royal Caribbean canceled a recent Alaska cruise after delays, leaving passengers stranded and disappointed in Vancouver with limited amenities.
item.content:encoded:
Passengers aboard a cruise ship preparing to set sail for Alaska were left scrambling recently after the cruise line abruptly canceled the trip — citing unspecified technical problems.

The seven-night Alaska cruise aboard Royal Caribbean’s Serenade of the Seas was scheduled to depart Vancouver, Canada, on Aug. 30 but had been delayed until Sept. 1 for maintenance, according to the blog "Cruise Critic." But the trouble didn't end there. 

Some two days after passengers embarked in Vancouver, Royal Caribbean reportedly announced that the voyage aboard Serenade of the Seas was canceled.

CRUISES THROWN INTO CHAOS AS DROUGHT STRANDS SHIPS, LEAVES PASSENGERS SCRAMBLING

Passengers were able to use the ship’s amenities as they worked on booking flights home, several cruise blogs reported.

The voyage was originally scheduled to stop in Sitka, Juneau, Ketchikan and Prince Rupert.

"To accommodate ongoing maintenance, we’ve had to cancel our sailing. We apologize to our guests for the inconvenience and have worked with them to adjust their travel plans," a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a shared statement.

"Repairs have now been completed, and the ship is ready to welcome guests on its next scheduled sailing," the spokesperson added.

The problem started on Aug. 22. Royal Caribbean emailed guests to inform them that the sailing would be reduced to five days to accommodate additional maintenance, "Cruise Critic" reported.

Guests who weren't interested in the shortened trip were given several options, including a refundable onboard credit and a future cruise credit, according to the blog.

The ship ultimately did not leave Vancouver because the repairs were not finished, the blog said. 

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

All booked passengers will receive a full refund, retain their previously issued onboard credit, receive a future cruise credit for 100% of their cruise fare and receive reimbursement for eligible flight-change fees, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported.

Serenade of the Seas, a mid-sized Royal Caribbean vessel, can accommodate 2,143 guests at double occupancy. 

The ship is known for its floor-to-ceiling windows that offer views of the surrounding scenery, alongside amenities like a rock-climbing wall, a glass-domed solarium and multiple dining venues.

The ship has experienced other technical difficulties in recent years. 

In July 2025, Serenade of the Seas experienced engine trouble soon after leaving Vancouver for a seven-night Alaska cruise, forcing it to return to port for overnight testing, several publications reported. 

The vessel set sail again the following evening, but passengers missed out on a planned stop in Sitka, Alaska.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Days earlier, technical problems on the ship's June 29 sailing had caused it to skip Icy Strait Point and scenic cruising in Tracy Arm Fjord, with those passengers receiving onboard credit equal to one day of their cruise fare.

Some passengers affected by the canceled Alaska cruise took to Reddit to express their frustration.

"This has been an immense disappointment. This was my girlfriend’s birthday cruise with my family and some family friends, and it has been an utter disaster and disappointment from start to finish," a Reddit user said.

"I was told [to] feel free to use my onboard credits on the ship — but for what? Only a few of the bars are open. None of the shops or casinos [are] open," a Reddit user said in another thread.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Oh my, what a disaster. Glad I canceled and didn’t board. Still waiting for my cruise fare refund, though," said another person. 

Several online commenters expressed sympathy for those inconvenienced by the cancellation, while others expressed apprehension about future trips they've booked with the line. 

One Reddit user asked what a group of eight can "absolutely not miss in Vancouver" as they planned to "enjoy the rest of the week and keep our flights home."

Serenade of the Seas welcomed passengers aboard again on Sept. 6 for its next seven-day, round-trip Alaska cruise, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported on Sept. 7.

item.title: Menendez brothers granted 2027 parole hearing a year earlier than expected
item.description: Erik and Lyle Menendez will face a parole hearing in March 2027, moved up from 2028 reportedly under Proposition 9 provisions after their resentencing.
item.content:encoded:
Erik and Lyle Menendez have been granted a parole hearing for next year, a year earlier than previously expected.

The brothers, who were both convicted of the Aug. 20, 1989, shotgun slayings of their parents, Jose and Mary Louise "Kitty" Menendez, in their Beverly Hills home, are scheduled to have a parole suitability hearing in March 2027 instead of August 2028, Fox News confirms. 

The change stems from two provisions included in Proposition 9, which allow a prison inmate's next parole hearing date to be moved up if there is a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole, The Orange County Register reported.

CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

"For almost 40 years, Erik and Lyle have worked to take responsibility for their actions, confront and heal from the unimaginable abuse and trauma they endured, grow as individuals, and dedicate themselves to serving others," a statement by family members reads.

"Through efforts such as helping to establish a hospice program and creating Green Space, they have sought to build an environment that reminds people serving life sentences that their lives still have meaning and that, regardless of their circumstances, they can choose each day to grow, heal, accept accountability, and contribute something of value to the world around them," they added.

NEW HAMPSHIRE RESENTENCING GIVES DARTMOUTH KILLER ROBERT TULLOCH A PAROLE PATH AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

The brothers were handed life sentences without the possibility of parole for the murders, which drew widespread media attention. However, they were resentenced to life in May 2025, making them eligible for parole.

The new sentencing came amid a push by supporters following a Netflix series on the case that resurrected calls for their freedom. They were denied parole last year.

NEVADA PAROLE BOARD REJECTS HENRY RUGGS III'S BID FOR EARLY RELEASE AFTER DEADLY 156 MPH DUI CRASH

The brothers have said the murders were committed after years of sexual abuse by their father. However, prosecutors have contested the claims, arguing the pair killed their parents out of greed.

"Erik and Lyle were once sentenced to life without the possibility of parole," the family statement said. "We will always be profoundly grateful that they have been resentenced and that our family can now imagine a future in which they are once again part of our everyday lives… We are incredibly proud of the men they have become and deeply grateful to the Parole Board for recognizing their efforts and allowing them to advance their parole hearing."

Lyle Menendez, 58, and Erik Menendez, 55, are both incarcerated in the Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility in San Diego.

item.title: Olivia Dunne pours beers like a patriot while her LSU tigers run up the score, Gator Bait & Lane's subtle shot
item.description: Lane Kiffin's LSU demolished Clemson as Olivia Dunne poured Miller Lites for fans, while Florida revived its controversial Gator Bait chant.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

"The Week 1 college football schedule stinks, the NCAA needs to try a little harder next time!"

Idiot. Goodness, I was an IDIOT Friday. That was my big gripe going into this glorious first weekend of college football.

The schedule wasn't great. On paper, it wasn't.

CLOCK CONTROVERSY ALLOWS MICHIGAN WOLVERINES TO AVOID MASSIVE UPSET AGAINST WESTERN MICHIGAN

Of course, college football games are played on the field, and they never, ever disappoint. Simpletons like myself look at the paper and see "Western Michigan-Michigan" and think we're in for a snoozer.

And then the Big Ten refs slap you across the face and tell you to SNAP OUT OF IT. What a game! What a weekend. And how about the Ole Miss-Louisville shootout from last night?

How lucky are we? How great is college football. Welcome back, old friend. Let's have a season.

Welcome to a Labor Day Nightcaps — the one where Olivia Dunne serves up booze while Lane Kiffin serves up an a–kicking to Clemson and poor Dabo Swinney.

Lordy, what a mismatch.

What else? I've got the Florida Gators reviving a lib-triggering chant, the field for last night's game in Nashville was disgraceful, and how great is the ESPN broadcasting team of Sean McDonough and Greg McIlroy?

I said it last year, and I'll say it again today: If those two are on a call, expect fireworks. Every time. It never fails.

OK, grab you one final summer beer before the unofficial calendar tuns to fall at 12 a.m., and settle in for a special holiday 'Cap!

Look, it's a holiday. You're all (hopefully) grilling/drinking/both right now, and paying very little attention to this class.

Trust me, I don't take it personally.

Because of that, we're gonna keep it short and simple. We all have things to do and more football to watch. Lord knows I do.

So, let's go ahead and get this Labor Day party started with Olivia Dunne returning to her roots and pouring some ice cold Miller Lites for the Tiger faithful before LSU absolutely annihilated Clemson on Saturday:

OutKick pointed this out months ago, but it's worth repeating today: Miller Lite partnering with Livvy Dunne to promote their beer was the smartest move a beer company has made in quite some time.

Look at the Bud Light fiasco from a few years back. I'm pretty sure Bud is still trying to recover. I'm not sure they ever fully will.

Miller saw that, took some notes, used their brains, and decided to bring in Olivia Dunne this year instead. It worked out perfectly with Lane Kiffin going to LSU, too.

Talk about a 1-2 punch!

Speaking of Lane at LSU ... those with good hearing caught this little remark during his halftime interview of Saturday's blowout win against Clemson:

Amazing.

Look, I'm no longer the biggest Lane Kiffin fan. I used to be, but the way he left Ole Miss last fall really turned me away. At this point, the proof is sort of in the pudding.

He will, inevitably, leave things in terrible shape. Tennessee. USC. Oakland. Ole Miss. There will always be drama.

That being said, he's still a #content machine.

Fair is fair, and that was a funny little one-liner at the end. Sure, it's a little silly given he's the one choosing to create all this NFL-college drama, but if his team's gonna go into the locker room up 31-3 at the half, he's welcome to talk all the crap he'd like.

And I'll eat it up.

OK, let's rapid-fire this quick holiday class into a big Labor Day night. First?

You know who is also a #content machine in the world of college football? New Florida coach Jon Sumrall.

Look at what this DEMON brought back to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday:

Goodness, did I miss that song! I grew up going to Gators games during the glory years ('98-2011), and that song was such a banger every time.

For those confused as to why the left deemed it racist ...

The former UF president canceled it back in 2020 because of what he deemed racist imagery and literature from way back in the early 1900s.

That imagery? Black children being used as bait to catch alligators. Yeah, disgusting. Not good.

Also, not at all associated with the Gator Bait chant. Literally no correlation!

"While I know of no evidence of racism associated with our ‘Gator Bait’ cheer at UF sporting events, there is horrific historic racist imagery associated with the phrase," former UF president Kent Fuchs wrote in a letter in June 2020.

Still, he bent the knee because the world went absolutely crazy during that horrible summer, and the Gator Bait chant had been locked away ever since.

Until this past weekend, when the fine folks in Gainesville dusted it off and unleashed it for the first time in six years.

Perfection. Sanity wins again!

Next? How great was Sean McDonough last night? I know Fowler and Herbie get all the shine, but I maintain that any time Sean McDonough is on the call for a college football game, it's destined to be electric:

Sean McDonough, by the way, is the only announcer I can think of who excels in not one, not two, but THREE sports.

He's a great baseball guy. I grew up listening to him call Red Sox games for WEEI, and he still does occasionally during the summer. Amazing.

He's also ESPN's hockey guy, and he nails it.

Obviously, he's done both college and the NFL. Don't forget, he took over for Tirico on Monday Night Football during a pretty down time for ESPN in terms of games. They used to get some pretty awful MNF games. That, of course, changed when Joe Buck and Troy Aikman came in a few years ago.

Weird!

My point? Sean McDonough probably deserves more praise than he gets. I'd put him up there with the best of the best. In terms of college football, there is no one better at the moment.

Frankly, it's not close.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Let's enjoy some football tonight. And Wednesday. And Thursday. And Friday. And Saturday. And Sunday.

And again, next Monday!

I just hope the fields don't look like this abomination from Tennessee last night:

Where does McDonough rank for you? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter turns $427 NCAA suspension into powerful cancer research fundraiser
item.description: Arion Carter is donating $427 per tackle to Nashville cancer charities after his girlfriend Mariah Bryant was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer.
item.content:encoded:
Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter walked out of the tunnel as the Vols’ sole captain during their home opener this past weekend, even though he was not suited up for the game.

Amid the controversial decisions surrounding former professional athletes returning to college athletics, Carter accepted his punishment when he could have easily sought help from a local judge to create a path back onto the field.

Following the 2025 season, the Vols linebacker decided to declare for the 2026 NFL Draft and leave Tennessee to pursue his professional dreams.

TENNESSEE COACH UNLOADS ON NCAA'S 'BULLS–T', AFTER STAR LINEBACKER SUSPENDED FOR OUTDATED RULE

Unfortunately, Carter found out he was dealing with a foot injury that would require him to have surgery and miss out on preparations for the upcoming draft. So, he made the decision to return to college.

There were a few complications. Carter accepted $427 from an agent to cover a flight to a workout, and he knew his return to Tennessee could lead to an NCAA suspension.

The NCAA's punishment came in the form of a one-game suspension that was initially set to keep the star linebacker out for the opening three games of the season.

With all of the chaos surrounding college athletics — from state courtrooms to federal court — Carter handled the situation with the utmost respect.

Arion's girlfriend is currently in the middle of her own battle with cancer.

To show his support, Carter recently shaved his head for the woman he loves. Mariah Bryant was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer earlier this year. She lives in the Nashville area, where she works as an ICU nurse at a local hospital.

But now, he's also raising money for cancer research with his play on the field. First reported by Austin Price of VolQuest, Arion Carter will donate $427 for each tackle that he makes this season to Nashville area charities that support women struggling to pay bills during their battles with cancer.

He is turning the $427 plane ticket reimbursement into something positive for the community, further demonstrating the character of a young man who has handled this entire ordeal with tremendous class.

Wearing a "Team Jesus" shirt on Monday, Carter explained how he is turning a negative situation into a positive one.

"It also goes back to my mom. She has always wanted a create a foundation, a non-profit for women and little girls," Carter reflected on Monday. "With my girlfriend, going what she's went though over these last few months, and me seeing it firsthand, it just really touched my heart and made me have a different perspective.

"I wanted to raise awareness and set up a foundation for cancer research and be able to do this. So, that was the origin of that."

In addition to the first amount, Carter will donate $500 for each sack recorded this season, along with $1,000 for every interception or forced fumble. If he ends up scoring a touchdown while on defense, he will donate $5,000 for cancer research.

COLLEGE ATHLETICS' LATEST MESS: COURT ORDERS SAY PRO ATHLETES CAN PLAY, BUT SEC AND BIG TEN READY TO FIGHT

"I think it’s indicative of who he is, right? He’s passionate about a cause for multiple reasons – obviously for his girlfriend and his family history, as well," Tennessee's Josh Heupel said Monday. "He’s a guy that cares about community, so it’s indicative of who he is as a person."

Although Carter repaid the $427 plane ticket, he was punished for declaring his intentions to enter the NFL Draft. While the rule may make sense on paper, the NCAA could have used this entire situation as a positive public-relations opportunity.

"I feel like some things you can't control," Carter said. "I feel like you have to take everything with a grain of salt, not be too bitter about certain situations because there are rules at the end of the day. Even if the rules may not seem they are fair in a sense, I can’t control them.

"This is another way for me to turn a negative into a positive and get the season started in a great way."

Now, the Tennessee linebacker is writing his own story on how this all played-out, with the Vols set to battle Georgia Tech this weekend in Atlanta in primetime.

Every time Carter makes a play, someone battling cancer will benefit from his outstanding character.

item.title: King Charles III clarifies Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not resume royal duties after UK move
item.description: Buckingham Palace reaffirmed that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not resume royal duties despite their UK return, keeping HRH titles in abeyance.
item.content:encoded:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle may be back on British soil, but their return home won’t come with a royal reset.

Buckingham Palace has drawn a firm line around the Sussexes’ homecoming, reaffirming that the couple will not resume official duties and that their status remains unchanged from when they stepped back as working royals in 2020.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family," a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III read, Fox News can confirm. "This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected."

The letter further underscored that a change in address does not mean a change in royal status.

PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE FACE RENEWED CRITICISM OVER ‘HALF-IN, HALF-OUT’ ROYAL ROLE: EXPERTS

"It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex," the letter added. "Their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and are not used. The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity. In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."

PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE'S UK RETURN SIGNALS ‘SPECTACULAR DEFEAT’ AS ROYAL EXPERTS WARN OF WILLIAM SHOWDOWN

The letter was sent by the Lord Chamberlain, the most senior official in the royal household, to senior officials in the government and military, as well as lord lieutenants, the king’s personal representatives around the country.

Fox News Digital reached out to a representative for Prince Harry and Markle for comment.

Markle and Prince Harry moved back to the U.K. in late August.

The couple’s children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, have already enrolled at British schools and will start classes sometime in September. The family plans to live at a private, nonroyal residence outside of London, but haven’t said exactly where that will be.

The couple won't return to any semblance of the life they held before, according to one royal expert.

"While Harry and Meghan are returning, they are not regaining official royal roles," British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "Nor was there any agreement to a 'half-in, half-out' construct. They have been thwarted by trying to do what they agreed to with Queen Elizabeth II."

If a return to royal duties was off the table, Harry's motivation for coming home could be far more personal.

Former butler to King Charles III, Grant Harrold, wondered if Harry's desire to spend more time with his father had shifted the prince's priorities after feeling homesick for some time.

But a return to Britain would put Harry and Meghan firmly back under the royal microscope, he warned, with both the public and the palace watching their every move.
